title: Making the Swedish band recording with earphones; no diary kept
summary: The interviewer praises his bitey solos; Holmes recalls playing along to tapes with earphones in 1975, regrets not keeping a diary and agrees the interviews preserve history.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: Record labels, producers and the business of making albums

blocks.x: No, well, you came through with some real solos and some fine...
Well, I don't know...
Yeah, it's got attack and bite and everything, I think. I think that's one of the better things you've done in recent years.
Yeah, that's what I'm afraid of. Somebody might attack me and bite me and everything else. But it was an experience.
Because I know you were worried that by playing the tapes and practicing, you might end up in the wrong key because of the speed of the tapes.
Yeah, that's right. That's right.
But your machine and their machine worked out so that the keys they set were the keys that your machine actually played. So that turned out to be no problem.
No, that was no problem.
Then as I remember it, I came and got you and we went down to the studio, and everything went very smoothly.
Yeah, well...
Holmes (12/5) - 58
You just had your earphones on there and you added your bits to the thing, and it came out as correspondent(?) with Charlie Holmes.
Yeah, yeah...
That was your last record, I think.
I wouldn't be surprised. I wouldn't be surprised. That was about 19....
'73, wasn't it?
'73 was my first one.
That was your first.
Yeah. And I think then '75 was the one you did with Kostbandet(?).
I never keep track of the dates. If I had known that I would be asked all these questions when I started out in life, then I would have...
Kept a diary.
Oh yeah. I would have kept a (?), you know.

Well, of course, that's what the purpose of this whole interview really is, and the other interviews that have been with other musicians, is to try to catch this material from the people who actually were there and who actually did the work, before it all disappears.
Holmes (12/5) - 59
Yeah. And things will disappear, believe me.
Well, we have to job whoever's memory we still have at our disposal.
Yeah...
[PAUSE]
